blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Managing logistics costs in practice means breaking the total bill into categories that a team can actually act on. Fuel is one line. Labour is another. Storage, handling, transport, returns, damage and exceptions each need their own line and their own owner. Without that split, 'logistics cost' is one big number that nobody can move.

Once the categories exist, the work becomes focused. Fuel is driven down by route discipline and carrier negotiation. Labour is driven by productivity and overtime control. Handling is driven by training and layout. Each category has its own levers, its own owner and its own weekly conversation.

Trim waste, combine trips, negotiate honestly, measure honestly — repeated every week, by the same small team, these habits reshape the cost base more reliably than any one-off programme.

items.q: According to the text, why can't anyone move 'logistics cost' when it is a single number?
options: Because fuel prices change too often
Because it is not split into categories a team can act on
Because the team is too small
items.why: "Without that split, 'logistics cost' is one big number that nobody can move."

items.q: What drives labour costs down, according to the text?
items.why: "Labour is driven by productivity and overtime control."

items.q: The text suggests that a one-off programme is…
options: less reliable than repeated weekly habits
the only way to cut fuel costs
items.why: Inferência: "these habits reshape the cost base more reliably than any one-off programme" — a rotina semanal supera a ação isolada.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: One large annual push does more than steady weekly work.
Fuel and labour respond to different levers.
Weekly discipline shapes the cost base over time.
Every cost category should have its own owner.
items.why: Inferência: o texto defende a disciplina semanal contra o "one-off programme" — o autor discordaria da opção 2.

items.q: Why does the author give each category its own owner and weekly conversation?
options: To make the total bill look larger
To reduce the number of categories
To make each cost line focused and actionable
items.why: Inferência: separar por dono e reunião semanal torna cada linha "focused" — alguém responde e age sobre ela.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie apresentando o novo mapa de custos à equipe de logística. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Okay, before I share the new sheet, let me explain why I rebuilt it. For years, 'logistics cost' was one line on the report. One number. And every time it went up, we argued about it, but nobody could actually do anything, because we couldn't see what was inside it.

So I split it. Fuel now has its own line and its own owner. Labour, storage, handling, returns and damage — each one has a name next to it and a target for the month. If fuel goes up, we know exactly who is looking at it and what they are trying with the carriers.

Here is what I want from each of you. Once a week, ten minutes, you bring your category. What moved, why it moved, and what you are doing about it next week. That's it. Trim the waste, combine the trips, negotiate honestly, measure honestly.

I know a single big project feels more exciting than a weekly ten-minute check. But honestly, the boring version is the one that works. Small, repeated, owned. That is how the cost base actually comes down.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why couldn't the team do anything when 'logistics cost' was one line?
options: The report was published too late
There was no budget for it
They couldn't see what was inside the number
items.why: "nobody could actually do anything, because we couldn't see what was inside it."

items.q: What does Sophie want from each person once a week?
options: A ten-minute update on their category: what moved, why, and next steps
items.why: "Once a week, ten minutes, you bring your category. What moved, why it moved, and what you are doing about it next week."

items.q: What does Sophie mean when she calls the weekly check 'the boring version'?
options: It is unexciting but it is the approach that actually works
It is unimportant and can be skipped
It is only for junior staff
items.why: Inferência: ela admite que é menos empolgante que um grande projeto, mas afirma que é o que funciona.

items.q: What can we infer about how Sophie sees a single big project?
options: She thinks it is the fastest way to cut costs
She believes it is the only serious option
She wants to launch one next month
She values steady weekly work over a one-off push, even if it feels less exciting
items.why: Inferência: "Small, repeated, owned. That is how the cost base actually comes down" — ela prefere a rotina ao projeto único.

items.q: How would you best describe Sophie's tone?
options: Practical and reassuring, asking for a small steady commitment
Uncertain about whether the plan will work
items.why: Inferência: ela explica o porquê, pede algo pequeno ("ten minutes") e reforça que funciona — tom prático e tranquilizador.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We gave each spending category a single owner." A category is…
options: a type or group of similar things
items.why: Category = categoria: um grupo ou tipo de itens semelhantes (fuel, labour, storage…).

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Fuel now has its own ___ on the cost report, separate from labour."
items.why: Line = linha: cada custo aparece na sua própria linha no relatório.

items.q: "Overtime pushed labour costs up last month." Overtime is…
options: the time a truck spends in storage
hours worked beyond the normal schedule, usually paid extra
items.why: Overtime = hora extra: horas além do horário normal, em geral pagas a mais.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Better route planning helped us ___ the waste out of our fuel bill."
items.why: To trim = aparar/cortar: reduzir aos poucos o desperdício do custo.

items.q: "These weekly habits slowly reshape the cost base." The cost base is…
options: the overall structure of a company's ongoing costs
the warehouse where costs are recorded
the price charged to the customer
items.why: Cost base = base de custos: o conjunto estrutural dos custos correntes da empresa.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de custos de logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The finance director still has to sign off on the new cost categories." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the weekly cost review to every depot next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implantar de forma progressiva, área por área.

items.q: "The warehouse team pushed back on the new overtime limit." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar por completo.

items.q: "They agreed to cut the fuel waste but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Trimming a few boxes won't move the needle on the total cost base." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer uma diferença perceptível.
